Commentary.Commentary: An interesting contest has come to an end! The men from Afghanistan have proved their mettle and shown a lot of maturity as well. The results are showing and they are advancing northwards pretty quickly. Bangladesh, on the other hand, have been disappointing. A complete performance was the need of the hour for them but their batting fizzed out again. They will be playing for pride on 7th of June in the final T20I at 2000 Local (1430 GMT) at this same venue. Will the Bangla Tigers come out reinvigorated? Or will the Men in Blue run away with the show? Do join us. Cheers!

Man of the Match, Rashid Khan, thanks the Almighty first up. Reckons that the team expects high standards from him so is happy to deliver whenever he can, whether it be with the bat, the ball or in the field. Informs that the plan was to bowl in a good length area and be disciplined, which eventually gave him success. Feels that Soumya Sarkar, Tamim Iqbal, Shakib Al Hasan and Mahmudullah were crucial wickets as a lot rests on them. Thanks the crowd for their support in these two games and hopes they will come out for the final clash as well.

Asghar Stanikzai says he's happy they won the series. Adds they know their strengths in the T20 format which plays to their advantage. States that the wicket was good for spinners, which is why his boys managed to do well. Thanks the crowd for coming out and providing support to his team and also sends out a word of thanks to the people supporting them back home in Afghanistan.

Shakib Al Hasan says they bowled and fielded well, but were 15-20 runs short. Mentions they got off to a good start with the bat but kept losing wickets and couldn't score runs in the middle overs. Applauds Afghanistan's spinners, especially Rashid Khan, for putting in a fantastic performance. Credits his pace bowlers for doing well and also acknowledges the effort put in by all his teammates.

The visiting team was on the money with the ball as well as in the field, but Shenwari was grinding it out. He batted with a lot of responsibility and kept on rotating the strike, also putting away the bad deliveries. Just when the run rate was creeping up, Nabi delivered the goods. He kept his composure and hit some lusty blows to take his side over the line. Earlier, a spirited bowling performance from the hosts saw them restricting the visitors to a below par score. Rashid Khan was the hero again as he picked up a 4-fer and choked the tourists' middle-order.

Afghanistan continue to rise through the ranks. Another clinical performance has seen them get the better of the opposition. They have won the first T20I series being contested between the two nations and are ecstatic! Credit to them for playing sensibly and putting in the hard yards on a track which had gone tackier. It was a steady start from the duo of Mohammad Shahzad and Usman Ghani but a couple of quick wickets brought Bangladesh back in the game.

SIX! Nabi finishes off in style! Afghanistan have sealed the 3-match T20I series here itself. Good length ball outside off, Nabi backs himself and launches it over wide long off. It is going, going and clears the fence with ease. Happy faces in the Afghan camp. AFGHANISTAN WIN BY 6 WICKETS!
FOUR! His mind is working like a computer at the moment! Similar delivery outside off, he was expecting it. Waits for it and ramps it over short third man for a boundary.
Play and a miss! Back of a length ball well outside off, Mohammad tries to hit it through the line but misses.

SIX! That shot has released the pressure completely! Nabi has been cool as a cucumber and he has delivered in a crunch situation. Only 10 more needed from 10 balls. In the arc for Nabi, he stays steady and heaves it way into the deep mid-wicket stands. Pressure is telling on Hossain.
FOUR! Drilled! Just what the doctor ordered for Afghanistan. Full ball in line of the stumps, Nabi hammers it over the head of the bowler for a rocketing boundary.
Shafiqullah Shafiq is the new man in. He played a gem of a cameo in the previous match. This is what is exactly needed from him again. Meanwhile, Rubel Hossain is back on.

OUT! Bowled 'em! Tossed up ball outside off, Shenwari tries to go big downtown but seems to have got an inside edge which has crashed into the stumps. Well, the umpire is not sure and he has a chat with his partner. It has been taken upstairs. It is not a drag on, in fact Shenwari missed it completely. A very vital breakthrough in the context of the game. Can Bangladesh win it from here?
What happened there? Looks like Shenwari has dragged it on. The umpire is confused. Let's find out...
SIX! Hammered! Brilliant shot. Shortish delivery, Shenwari lines it up and powers it over long on for a biggie.
On the shorter side, Nabi drags his pull to deep mid-wicket for a run.
The batsman plays the pull shot. They pick up a single.

A huge appeal has been turned down. Drifting in, Shenwari shapes for the sweep but misses to get hit on the pads. Bangladesh are confident but the umpire shakes his head. Might have just slipped down leg.
Flatter delivery, drilled to long on for a single.
FOUR! Innovative! Afghanistan are well and truly in the game. Shenwari is playing a very responsible knock. Full on middle, reverse swept over short third man to find the fence.
Quick, fast and accurate, Shenwari shapes for the cut but only drags it down the track.
Fired in this time, Shenwari is cramped for room and only manages a bottom edge.
On a flatter trajectory on middle, pulled away through mid-wicket for a couple.
Nabi uses his feet and Shakib shortens his length. Clipped to mid-wicket for a run.
Coming in with the arm, driven towards mid off for a single.
Outside off, cut away to sweeper cover for a single. The hosts need 37 from 24 balls.

SIX! Boom! This was really needed. Short ball on middle and leg, Shenwari picks up the length quickly and pulls it with aplomb over square leg. Has hit it really well and the ball sails into the stands.
Tries to innovate but fails! A dot ball is worth in gold now. Quick outside off, Shenwari tries the paddle scoop but is beaten.
Slower through the air, chipped over mid on for a single.
Short ball, pulled away to deep mid-wicket for a single.

Another leg before has been turned down!  Spinning down the leg side, Shenwari tries to hit it out of the ground but gets hit on the pads. An appeal ensues but it is of no use. It was probably going down leg.
Shorter in length, tucked to the man at 45 for a run. A brilliant spell from Islam has come to an end. His figures read - 4-2-14-0.
Floated delivery, Nabi works it towards mid on for a quick single. They need boundaries now.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Nicely done! Straight this time, Nabi kneels and sweeps it wide of short fine leg to find the fence.
Sits deep in the crease and turns it to the leg side for a run.
Wide! Bowls this one wide outside off, left alone.
Tossed up ball, knocked down to long on for a run.
Nazmul Islam is back on.
Goes back and punches this one for a single.
Hangs back to this one and punches it out.
Mohammad Nabi is the new man in.

OUT! Gone! The skipper departs without making any sort of impact. Hossain bowls this one wider outside off. Stanikzai comes down the track and tries to tonk it across the line but misses it completely. Rahim collects the ball and takes the bails off in a flash. It has been taken upstairs but the Bangladeshi players are already celebrating. The replays confirm that the batsman has failed to put his bat down in the crease. The pressure is building up.
Stanikzai looks a goner! There is a stumping appeal in question. The umpire wants to be sure though.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single.

A big, big appeal for an LBW denied! Shorter in length, Stanikzai uses his feet and tries to hit it across but misses to get hit on the pads. Hossain is confident but the umpire shakes his head. That was probably going down leg.
On middle and leg, turned through mid on for a single.
Mosaddek Hossain into the attack.
Flatter, shorter and outside off, Asghar opens the face and runs it down to short third man. Wants the run but then has to abort it.
Short and wide outside off, cut square on the off side for a single.
Shifts his weight onto his back foot and punches it down the ground to long on for a single.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.

Tossed up delivery on the stumps, Stanikzai sweeps it in front of square leg. The fielder out in the deep has to rush to his right and cover a lot of ground to stop it, does so and keeps the batsmen down to two.
Short in length with not much spin on it, punched down to long off for a single.
Shakib Al Hasan back on.
Works it away through the vacant mid-wicket area for a single. 64 runs to win in 48 balls.
SIX! He's got enough on that. Dropped short, Shenwari sees the opportunity to put this away so he rocks back in a jiffy and muscles it over long on. Just over the fielder, much-needed hit.
Drifting away outside off, goes back and offers a firm punch to covers. Both batsmen set off for a run, but then decide against it.
Short and wide outside off, cut square to deep backward point for a single.
From around the wicket, it's darted full in length, Stanikzai wrists it to the right of the bowler. Can't beat him though as Mahmudullah quickly dives low to his right and stops it.
On a driving length, outside off, pushed towards mid off for a quick run.
Mahmudullah comes on to bowl. Also, Rubel Hossain is going off the field. He seems to have hurt himself on the last delivery while trying to stop that.
Driven through mid off for a single. Rubel got low to stop that, made a half-stop back down the ground. 73 needed in 54 now.

Huge, huge shout for a leg before, turned down by the umpire. Rubel lands it on a length on middle and leg, it comes back in and catches Shenwari on the pads who misses his flick. Big appeal, but it's going down leg. So good decision from the umpire.
FOUR! Short of a good length on the stumps, Shenwari pulls it firmly through mid-wicket. Beats the diving fielder out in the deep and earns himself a boundary.
Asghar Stanikzai is the new man in.

OUT! He hasn't and Ghani is out of here. He was struggling throughout the innings, departs finally. Shortish in length and around off, Ghani swings hard, looking to slap it over covers but gets it off the splice. Lobs it towards mid off where Sarkar moves to his left and takes a good diving catch. The umpire takes it upstairs, just to make sure if Hossain overstepped or not, and replays show he hasn't.
The umpire is checking whether Hossain overstepped his line or not.
Banged in short again, angling in this time, pulled to fine leg for a single.
Pounds it on short, just outside off, Shenwari goes for the big pull shot but the bounce gets the better of him.

Similar ball, pulled away to the leg side for a run. Afghanistan are 56/1 at the end of 10 overs whereas Bangladesh were 81/3. Though the hosts have more wickets in hand, the surface seems to have got tackier. They still need 79 runs to win.
Another short ball as has been the trend, pulled away nicely to deep mid-wicket for a run.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Once again a mishit from Shenwari. Short ball, no sort of timing on that one as the ball goes towards mid-wicket. A run taken.
A bouncer angled in towards the body, Ghani pulls it towards deep mid-wicket for a run. Need to keep rotating the strike.
Pitched up delivery outside off, driven with hard hands towards mid off.
Full outside off, driven to the cover area for no run.
Short ball down the leg side, Shenwari attempts another pull but makes no contact. Rahim takes it and appeals casually. There was no wood involved. One for the over signaled by the umpire.
Back of a length ball, staying a bit low. Shenwari adjusts in his crease to pull it nicely to deep mid-wicket. A brace taken.
Hossain hits the deck hard and bowls a well-directed ball on middle and leg. The ball gets big on Ghani who attempts a pull but mistimes it towards short fine leg. A run taken.
Another dot ball, this is what is needed from the visitors' point of view. Tight stump-to-stump line, helped towards mid-wicket.
Good fielding! This is what Bangladesh need to do. On a length on middle, Ghani tucks it towards short mid-wicket where the fielder dives to his right to make a good stop.
Rubel Hossain is back on.
Short delivery this time, Samiullah ducks under it.
Straying on the pads, helped away to the leg side for a run.

Safe! Length delivery on middle and leg, Shenwari tries to hit it hard towards deep mid-wicket but only manages an inside edge onto his pads. Calls his partner through who responds immediately. Hider hares towards the ball, dives and underarms a direct hit on the stumps as Ghani dives full length to get home. It has been referred upstairs. The replays are in and the batsman is comfortably in. Full marks for the effort though.
Good work from Hider! He has hit the bull's eye at the striker's end but Shenwari seems to be safe. Let's find out...
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Wide! Hider loses his radar and slips this one down the leg side. Ghani misses his flick shot.
Straying on the hips this time, Usman hops and helps it nicely through square leg. A couple taken.
Well bowled! Good length delivery coming in from outside off, Ghani tries to play a deft touch towards third man but gets beaten.
Fuller in length this time, kept out watchfully. Another tidy over from Islam, only 5 singles from it.
Similar delivery, Usman goes deep in the crease and powers it towards long off. A run taken.
Slower in pace, knocked down to long off to change ends.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Sliding in with the arm, turned towards square leg to rotate strike.
Shorter in length, Ghani hangs back and punches it down to long on for a single. First run scored off Islam's bowling on his 13th delivery.
Nazmul Islam is back on.
Fuller in length this time, played with soft hands towards mid off. A decent Powerplay for Afghanistan and they are on track to hunt this total down.
Shaping in and induces an inside edge from Shenwari's bat.
Najibullah Zadran comes out to bat.

OUT! Plumb in front! This time Hider hits his mark and reaps the dividends. He runs in from around the wicket and angles in a good length ball. Shahzad doesn't have any space to work it away and tries to block it tamely. However, he misses it and is struck on the pads. Hider roars in an appeal and the umpire obliges. The visitors need to keep picking up wickets to put pressure on the opposition.
Two Wides! Slips this one down the leg side, Usman tries to work it away but misses. A slight fumble from Rahim allows the batsmen to take an extra run.
An effort ball from Hider. It is banged in and Ghani ducks under it.
Fullish delivery, shaping in, Ghani defends it solidly.
Erring in line, this time it is on the pads. Ghani works it nicely through square leg and picks up a couple for doing so.
Abu Hider comes in for a burst.
SIX! Well played! Shortish delivery, coming in with the angle at a quick pace. Shahzad goes back in a jiffy and smashes it over long on for a maximum.
Slow through the air, slog swept to the same region to rotate strike.
Shahzad is nimble on his feet and whips this one to deep mid-wicket. A run taken.
Floated delivery, defended solidly off the front foot.
FOUR! Powerful! He certainly packs a punch. Fullish in length and it is flighted as well. It allows Shahzad to get underneath it and whack it over the bowler to find the fence.
Coming in with the angle, knocked down to long on for a run.
Shakib Al Hasan is back on.
It has been a great comeback from Hossain after being hit for a boundary early in the over. Sees Mohammad using his feet and follows him. Cramps up the batsman and he can only block it.
Short delivery, climbing on Ghani who pulls it away unconvincingly to the leg side. Gets a run for doing so.
Leg bye! The batsman fails to get bat on that one and is hit on the pad. One run added to the total. The umpire signals a leg bye.

FOUR! Two boundaries in a row, this time albeit in a streaky manner. Shaping in substantially from a length, Shahzad comes down the track and swings aimlessly but gets an inside edge past the leg stump and through to the fine leg fence.

FOUR! Shahzad is unorthodox but he is really good at it as well. How efficient you are is what matters. Good length ball, angling in, Shahzad backs away, uses his feet and smashes it over covers for a rocketing boundary.
Back of a length outside off, slapped away to the man at point.
Rubel Hossain comes into the attack.
Fullish delivery down the leg side, Ghani turns it to the man at 45. Two maidens on the trot for Nazmul Ismal, it has been a dream start.
Quick and flat on off, kept out watchfully.
Hurrying the batsman with his pace, cut away just in the nick of time towards point.
A bit shorter in length and on a flatter trajectory, dealt with from within the crease.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Slows it through the air, Usman comes forward and defends it.
Coming in with the arm, tucked with the angle to mid on for a single.
Played to the point region by the batsman. One run added to the total.
FOUR! Clean as a whistle! Tossed up delivery, Shahzad makes room and lifts it over extra cover. Has made really good connection and the ball goes over the rope after bouncing once.
Similar length ball, punched past mid on for a run.

FOUR! Deft touch! Afghanistan are finally away after 7 deliveries. A touch on the shorter side outside off, Ghani waits for it and guides it late past the right side of the diving short third man fielder. Gets the desired result as well.
Starts off with a fullish ball outside off, driven crisply to the man at mid off.
Shakib Al Hasan to bowl from the other end.
A maiden over! Excellent start provided by Nazmul Islam. On middle and leg, slightly shorter in length, Shahzad punches it straight to short mid-wicket.
Shorter in length again, another defensive shot from the batsman.
4 dots in a row. Could... no... Should have been a wicket along with that. Around off, Shahzad blocks.

Dropped! No, no, no. That was the start Bangladesh needed and Rahim has put this down. Islam does well by bowling it around off, it turns away and takes a thin edge as Shahzad pokes at it. The keeper can't keep a hold of it.
Goes fuller this time, outside off. Pushed away off the front foot to covers.
From around the wicket, it's quicker and shorter, coming in on middle and leg, Shahzad goes back and punches it back to the bowler.
We are back for the second half. The Tigers need early wickets if they are to win this game. Mohammad Shahzad and Usman Ghani stride out to bat, as Nazmul Islam takes the ball first up. Here we go...
